_doc: CROSS-LANGUAGE reflect contract. The ts kernel (tests/reflect.test.ts) and the python kernel must BOTH reproduce every case's `expect` from `tree`+`bundles`. Edit here once; both runtimes re-verify. This is what keeps a second kernel from drifting. NOTE: the root reflect carries a per-runtime `runtime` field ("python"|"rust"|"swift"|"ts"); this fixture is exercised by the ts kernel so the root cases expect "ts". The root also carries deployment context `env` + `version` (read from FANTASTIC_ENV / FANTASTIC_VERSION on the host runtimes; the browser ts kernel has no env, so it is always env="host", version=null). Every reflect also carries `kernel_verbs` (#26): advertised on EVERY agent, answered by the root only. The ts kernel advertises the three verbs IT answers (ps/cancel/ledger) — python/rust/swift additionally list the tree-CRUD verbs they own, because this kernel genuinely has none: its tree is built by its bundles and persisted through the host loader, and advertising a verb it cannot answer would be a lie the model pays for. Every agent also carries the structural authority baseline {$self,$parent,$children} on BOTH `can_call` and `callable_by`, stamped and merged in the Agent constructor and surfaced by reflect (#7) — readable authority, so an agent is not left discovering its own reach by trial.

expect.sentence: Fantastic kernel. Everything is reachable by sending messages to agents.

kernel_verbs._: Kernel-owned: send to 'kernel'. The id you name is the OPERAND, not the actor. (`verbs` is what this agent itself does.) This kernel answers the three below; tree CRUD lives on the HOST root, reached over the bridge.
kernel_verbs.ps: args: limit:int?, after:str? — lists the LIVE dispatches (id, agent, verb), paged.
kernel_verbs.cancel: args: task_id:str — kills that task AND ITS SUBTREE; returns {cancelled, killed:[ids]}. An unknown or finished id kills nothing and says so.
kernel_verbs.ledger: args: limit:int?, after:str? — every execution YOU originated and what it became (id, target, status, attempts, retries, named); terminal non-completed rows ARE the dead-letter queue. Origin-scoped: an agent never sees another's rows.
